etymologies.etymologyHTML: From some +‎ where.

definitions.definition: In an uncertain or unspecified location.
To an uncertain or unspecified location.
Unspecified or unknown (unlocated) place or location.

quote.citation: 1986, Joel S. Goldsmith, A Parenthesis in Eternity: Living the Mystical Life, page 100:
quote.text: We have come from somewhere and we are going somewhere, but because life is an unending circle, we are again going to come from a somewhere, and we are again going to go to a somewhere, and this will go on, and on, and on.

quote.citation: 2008, Bill Watkins, The Once and Future Celt, page 283:
quote.text: A courting owl hoots in the somewheres of the night and another answers its call further off.

quote.citation: 2012, Thomas M. Kitts, Finding Fogerty: Interdisciplinary Readings of John Fogerty, page 6:
quote.text: […]  and it transports the person to a somewhere, a somewhere that the music dictates.

quote.citation: 2015 November 1, Clare Brennan, “The Oresteia review – strong performances at odds with the setting”, in The Observer‎[1]:
quote.text: This is essentialised place: a somewhere that is nowhere and yet everywhere.

definitions.definition: A person with strong cultural or social ties to a specific place.
